blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Rights are justiciable in nature and directly enforceable by courts.
Reasonable restrictions can be imposed on these rights by the State.
During a National Emergency, Fundamental Rights can be suspended except for Articles 20 and 21.
The Right to Property was converted from a Fundamental Right to a legal right under Article 300A by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.
Article 12 defines the term 'State' to include Central and State governments, Parliament, State Legislatures, Local Authorities, and other authorities within India.
Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.
Right to Property is no longer a Fundamental Right; it became a legal right under Article 300A via the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
Exams frequently ask to identify entities included in the definition of 'State' under Article 12 (Central/State governments, Parliament, Legislatures, Local Authorities, etc.).

blocks.content:
For Fundamental Rights, the term 'State' includes:
• Central Government
• State Governments
• Parliament
• State Legislatures
• Local Authorities
• Other authorities within Indian territory

Questions are often asked to identify what is included in the State.
